## Fixed

- **Fast-lane changes can reach the review gate again.** `reconcileStatuses` skipped every
  brainstorm whose lane wasn't `full`, on the stated theory that a fast-lane brainstorm has no
  change to reconcile against. The fast lane as it actually runs does write a change directory and
  a proposal — and the skip was not harmless: the post-Propose gate check only opens the gate for a
  brainstorm whose status is `proposed`, so **every fast-lane change dead-ended at "Propose doesn't
  look finished" with no gate ever offered**.

  Measured on `readyset-bench` label `b1-subset-0.12` (4 tasks × 3 reps, readyset arm alone):

  | stored lane | brainstorm status | gate shown |
  |---|---|---|
  | `full` | `approved` | 7 / 7 runs |
  | `fast` | `open` | 0 / 5 runs |

  A perfect split with no exceptions. This is the actual source of the historical T11/T12 "gate
  bypass": the gate was never shown, so the only way those runs reached code was the model
  continuing on its own. (The current harness refuses to auto-answer that stray text, which is why
  those runs now stop honestly as `gate-not-shown`.)

  The reconciliation now derives from the filesystem alone — the existing `changeState` guard
  already leaves a fast-lane brainstorm with no change directory untouched, so the lane filter was
  buying nothing.

- **That failure message now names the real cause.** It said "readyset/changes/…/proposal.md not
  found or empty" for all three failing conditions — no matching brainstorm, status not `proposed`,
  or an empty proposal. The middle case is what actually happens for a fast-lane change, and the
  wording sent a live investigation hunting for a file that was on disk the entire time.

Three new tests pin the behavior: a fast-lane brainstorm with a real change directory is
reconciled to `proposed`; one with no change directory is still left untouched; the full lane is
unchanged. The first fails against the old skip.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/fresp/readyset-flow/compare/0.12.0...0.12.1
